chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: The Alabam in the 1920s, the Depression and Mosby's departure
summary: Mosby's best days were the 1920s, including a visit by the Prince of Wales; in the Depression the place turned over owners and Mosby went to Oakland.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, during the '40s, I heard--I think it was the '40s--somebody told me William Randolph Hearst used to come down to the Alabam, and Orson Welles used to come to the Alabam and a lot of movie people would come down to see the shows.

Yeah. I think one night there they had the Prince of Wales there, you know. He become king afterwards, you know. And they...see, Mosby's big days was in the '20s. See? After the '30s when...like when Heflin and I took over, the thing would be vacant for a month or two...nobody runnin' it at all, and we go in there, and if we didn't make some money and didn't have no money, we couldn't pay rent, we'd be out, and then somebody else'd try again, and the Depression was on. The Depression started around '28...'29. See? So, we'd...those guys... they'd have four or five owners in three or four years. See? Because all you could do's go in there and rent it for two, three...a month or two, see how you come out, and if you didn't promote somethin', you was broke, you'd have to close down again.
Mosby left right at the beginning of the Depression, right? He left the Alabam?
Yeah, I think so, and he went up to Oakland, and he died up in Oakland. He opened up a place up there in Chinatown, I think...I heard.
